summary: Joseph Walker Jasper Ouseley was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as professor at Fort William College (1825), professor of Arabic and Persian at East India Company College (1844-1859), and Civil Service Commission examiner (1862-1883).

Joseph Walser works in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini. He was affiliated with Loyola University Chicago (attested 1998) and Tufts University (attested 1999-2001, and as associate professor in 2015).

Joseph Wright was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University under Hermann Osthoff, also studying at Yorkshire College and Leipzig. At Oxford, he served as lecturer (1888), deputy professor (1891-1901), and Professor of Comparative Philology (1901-1925).

Joseph van den Gheyn worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics, studying at KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He taught at Collège Saint-Michel, held the Sanskrit chair at Institut Catholique de Paris (1889), and served at the BnF (1897-1912).

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall was an Iranian, Central Asian, and history scholar who studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789-1799). He founded Fundgruben des Orients and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847-1849).
Josho Nozawa, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held a professorship at Koyasan University (attested 1950).

Joshu Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Zuiryo-ji under Joten Soko Miura. He served as abbot at Yotoku-in (1948-1953), Shojuan (1953), and Mount Baldy Zen Center, which he founded and led until 2012.
Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at McMaster University as a Ph.D. candidate under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn (attested 2026).

Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794-1799), studied under Johannes Lassar (~1805-1812), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua Timothy Katz is a linguist who earned his B.A. from Yale, M.A. from Oxford, and Ph.D. from Harvard. He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998-2022) and became a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (~2022).
Joshua W. C. Cutler works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

Joshua Whatmough was a linguist who studied at the University of Manchester and Emmanuel College. He served as lecturer in classics at Bangor University (1921-1925), professor of Latin at Cairo University (1925-1926), and professor at Harvard University from 1926.

Josiah Royce was a philosopher who earned his degrees at the University of California and Johns Hopkins, also studying under Hermann Lotze at Göttingen. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878-1882) before serving on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

Josip Florschütz was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1882-1885). In 1908, he was appointed extraordinary professor for comparative IE linguistics and related languages at the University of Zagreb.

José Alemany y Bolufer was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Pedro Roca y López and earned a doctorate from Complutense University of Madrid. He held chairs of Greek at the University of Granada (1891) and Complutense University (~1899-1934).

José Canedo Grille was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Seminario Mayor de Santiago de Compostela, the University of Granada, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding a post at Heidelberg University in 1943.

José Carlos Ribeiro Calazans Duarte is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar with degrees from the University of Lisbon, Sorbonne Nouvelle, EPHE, and Lusófona University. He served as a Ministry of Education teacher (1981-1995) and Lusófona assistant professor (2006-2021).

José Ignacio Cabezón specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. After earning his Ph.D. at Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, he taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1990-2001) and became Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.

José Ventura Traveset was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He served as professor of humanities at the University of Granada (1887-1889) and as professor at the University of Valencia (1901).
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).
